title: Excalidraw: AI and Human Whiteboarding Partnership - Christopher Chedeau
talk_summary: Christopher Chedeau recounts building Excalidraw and then walks through which AI integrations worked and which failed. The core lesson is that LLMs are far more reliable when they emit a structured domain-specific language (Mermaid) that deterministic code then renders, rather than emitting the final artifact directly, and that AI output should be a 90%-good starting point a human then edits.

takeaways.technique: LLM emits a DSL, deterministic code renders it
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asking the LLM to produce the final drawing (SVG/canvas/Excalidraw JSON), they have it generate Mermaid diagram syntax, then a hand-written Mermaid-to-Excalidraw backend converts that into native editable objects.
takeaways.evidence_quote: LLM's love structure. So if you're able to take your problem domain problem space and find a way to represent it in some kind of domain specific language

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat AI generation as producing a ~90% draft that lands as native editable objects, so a human (or downstream step) can fix layout/colors instead of being stuck with an opaque image.
takeaways.evidence_quote: no longer going to be like one shot. Hey, I'm asking the eye something and the eye give me like something perfect, but how do you get something that's close enough and then you as a human can start modifying

takeaways.technique: Don't ship a model just because it exists
takeaways.what_they_do: They tried an image-generation model and LLM-drawn diagrams, found users didn't draw realistic images and LLM diagrams were unusable, and dropped them; only kept integrations that measurably helped the task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just because there's a model that exists doesn't mean that it should be within your product

takeaways.what_they_do: They shipped small scoped AI features that LLMs are reliably good at (auto-naming documents after content exists, generating illustrations) rather than broad generative features.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one of the things that LM can actually really good at is generating names for these documents
